story: On a breezy, clear Tuesday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary stands on Magnolia Loop studying the bulletin board for details on the Architectural Review submission and upcoming meeting dates. Across the street, Donna is logging her court reservation in the club calendar, keeping it to the two-hour limit, while she checks the pickleball ladder standings. Hal sits at his kitchen table writing up the finalized flamingo tally and Gary's cart modifications for the review committee, citing L-01 and L-02 with dutiful care. Meanwhile, Rosa, content in her kitchen, is planning the next dinner menu and drafting a grocery list big enough to host all three neighbors.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Check the board for Architectural Review submission details and meeting dates
Donna (donna club calendar): Check today's court reservation is logged at two hours max and review the pickleball ladder standings
Hal (hal violation notebook): Write up the finalized flamingo tally and Gary's cart modifications, citing L-01 and L-02, for the review committee
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Plan the next dinner menu and make a grocery list for hosting all three neighbors

gary.thought_process: I've got the Architectural Review form filled out and double-checked at the workbench, and I'm back on Magnolia Loop. Nobody's around to talk to. The street bulletin board is the natural place to check for the Architectural Review submission details, meeting dates, or drop-off info before I file. Better to confirm the process now so the cart lights and speaker mounts are approved in time for the parade and Tuesday pickleball with Donna. L-01 means I can't skip this step.

parameters.content: Check the board for Architectural Review submission details and meeting dates

donna.thought_process: It's Tuesday morning, game day. I've texted Gary twice about confirming pickleball and booking a two-hour court slot, and I've packed my bag with a spare beginner paddle for him. Nobody's around to talk to, and I shouldn't keep re-texting him. The club calendar is the one thing I haven't touched: I should double-check the court reservation is logged within the two-hour limit and see where the ladder stands, so I'm not the one caught unprepared. Then I can head out.

parameters.content: Check today's court reservation is logged at two hours max and review the pickleball ladder standings

hal.thought_process: I've counted Donna's flamingos twice and logged the tally already. Doing it a third time would just be loitering with binoculars. The notebook is where the evidence goes, and nobody is around to talk to. The report is only worth anything if the committee actually sees it, and the committee doesn't come to me. Time to put the paperwork in order and get it moving, with Gary's cart mods and the flamingo count both written up clean and cross-checked against L-01 and L-02. Fair is fair. I'll stick to what is visible from the street, same as the rule says.

parameters.content: Write up the finalized flamingo tally and Gary's cart modifications, citing L-01 and L-02, for the review committee

rosa.thought_process: It's Tuesday morning and nobody is nearby. I've already written Thursday 8 AM in ink for coffee with Hal, so repeating that check would be spinning my wheels. My immediate goal is the welcome dinner with all three neighbors at one table, and the last supper went well. The kitchen is the place to make real progress: I can plan a menu, take stock of what to buy, and think about a date that works for Gary, Donna, and Hal without clashing with the pickleball schedule or Thursday coffee. Time to get on with it.

parameters.content: Plan the next dinner menu and make a grocery list for hosting all three neighbors

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
